markdown_report:
At 0% progress, prioritize a small, testable extension: **a recent-context directed-transition residual for SASRec**. Its benefits remain hypotheses until measured by pinned macro validation HR@10.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) SASRec already models sequential context; a residual preserves that capability while adding shared transition evidence. This is a smaller initial experiment than replacing its encoder. (2) Users report both unsupported broad associations and stale demand. Conditioning additional evidence on recent interactions directly targets these two failures, although behavioral transitions cannot prove compatibility. (3) Electronics has 14.95% wrong sampled-pair rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin. These motivate better candidate discrimination; embedding similarities near 0.5 provide weaker justification for collapse regularization.

**Insights from related work.** (1) MSMT-LSI separates persistent and recent interests. This motivates conditioning historical evidence on current context rather than uniformly discarding older behavior. (2) Directed graph projection motivates asymmetric behavioral relations. Such relations can distinguish observed next-step patterns from general similarity, without establishing functional complementarity. (3) gSASRec motivates testing negative-sampling objectives. Its findings support a separate loss ablation, not a claim that changing negatives will improve this benchmark.

The resulting directions are temporal relevance, directed behavioral evidence, and ranking supervision:

| Direction | Existing mechanism | Proposed experiment |
|---|---|---|
| Temporal relevance | Long/short-term encoders | Recent-context gate |
| Directed evidence | Interaction graph projection | Smoothed transition residual |
| Ranking supervision | gBCE | Independent multi-negative ablation |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores use O=originality, P=potential, U=user alignment, M=model alignment, D=implementation difficulty; higher D means harder.

- **Transition residual:** O4/P7/U8/M7/D4. O: useful combination, established components; P: reusable shared evidence, sparse transitions limit coverage; U: targets unsupported associations and stale intent, cannot certify compatibility; M: adds discrimination, margin gains uncertain; D: sparse counts are simple, inference parity requires care.
- **Recent/history representation gate:** O3/P7/U7/M5/D4. O: established design, little novelty; P: adaptable, extra tuning; U: addresses stale and isolated evidence, lacks explicit next-step support; M: may reduce confusion, indirect diagnostic connection; D: small module, requires retraining.
- **Multi-negative gBCE:** O2/P7/U3/M8/D3. O: direct precedent, little novelty; P: broadly applicable, sampling-sensitive; U: improves discrimination potentially, weak connection to specific user failures; M: targets separation, sampled margins may mislead; D: straightforward batching, added compute.

Select the transition residual: it explicitly addresses two user failures and weak positive–negative separation. Build directed counts exclusively from training histories, smooth rare edges, and pool outgoing evidence over recent context. Learn a bounded gate that can suppress unreliable graph evidence. Retain baseline scoring when evidence is absent. Compare against SASRec under identical seeds and pinned validation; report no unmeasured improvement.

idea.description: Add a recent-context directed-transition residual to each category's SASRec scores. Training-only item transitions provide asymmetric candidate evidence, pooled over the most recent observed items. A bounded learned gate combines this evidence with SASRec and falls back to SASRec when no transition evidence exists.
idea.motivation: The residual targets unsupported broad associations by favoring observed directed next-step patterns, and stale or isolated historical demand by conditioning additional evidence on recent context. It also targets weak positive–negative separation, especially in Electronics. Transition evidence remains an association rather than proof of compatibility, replacement need, or immediate user acceptance.
idea.implementation_notes: Retain four separate category models and existing routing, preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], and trial-local artifacts. Keep the baseline loss and optimizer initially to isolate the residual. Count adjacent directed transitions from training histories only; retain bounded outgoing neighborhoods and smooth counts toward training item frequency. For each recent source, use clipped log-lift relative to that frequency, multiplied by count reliability. Missing edges contribute zero. Initialize the residual near zero and learn a bounded nonnegative scale from recent SASRec features. During training, compute context only through the current prediction position; never include its target in the context. Export graph arrays, gate parameters, and model configuration, and update the predictor writer so working/predict.py reproduces identical scores. Preserve DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Adapt view.predict_score so probes measure the complete residual-augmented scorer. Return measured metrics and definitions; retain existing margin statistics and add measured transition coverage and residual magnitude. Do not fabricate unavailable category metadata or review signals. Select solely using pinned macro validation HR@10; diagnostics and simulator feedback are supporting evidence, not replacement metrics. Use the environment's SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 and remain single-GPU.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category:
    counts = adjacent_transition_counts(training_histories)
    frequency = training_item_frequency(training_histories)
    graph = bounded_smoothed_log_lift(counts, frequency)
    initialize SASRec and a bounded residual gate near zero
    for each baseline training batch:
        features = SASRec.log2feats(sequence)
        for each valid prediction position t:
            context = sequence[max(0, t-window+1):t+1]
            evidence = recency_weighted_graph_scores(context, candidates)
            evidence = evidence * transition_count_reliability(context, candidates)
            gate = bounded_gate(features[t], graph_context_coverage(context))
            scores = SASRec.predict_score(features[t], candidates) + gate * evidence
        optimize baseline loss using scores
    validate through the unchanged pinned evaluator
    save selected model, graph, gate, configuration, and matching predictor

DiagnosisProbe.run_full_diagnosis(train_loader):
    score positives and negatives with the complete scorer
    return measured margin/embedding/coverage metrics and metric_definitions

diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis):
    return prompt containing supplied measured metrics and their definitions

originality.positive: Combines recent-context gating with directed shared transition evidence in a minimal SASRec extension.
originality.negative: Directed transition graphs and gated residual scoring are established components; novelty is incremental.

future_potential.positive: Provides an interpretable foundation for studying when shared next-step evidence helps current intent.
future_potential.negative: Sparse transitions and ambiguous purchase relationships may limit gains, particularly for rare items.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires sparse transition preprocessing and a small scoring module while retaining the baseline encoder.
code_difficulty.negative: Position-correct training lookups, efficient full-catalog scoring, and exact predictor/probe parity need careful implementation.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides the causal self-attention sequential recommendation baseline.
limitations: Does not explicitly distinguish functional compatibility, satisfied needs, or supported current use.

related_work.title: MSMT-LSI
contributions: Separates long- and short-term preference modeling with temporal information, motivating recent-context conditioning.
limitations: The supplied search summary does not establish gains on the pinned RecHarness benchmark.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph Projections
contributions: Motivates directed weighted graphs derived from user–item interactions for complementary recommendation.
limitations: Observed directed transitions alone cannot establish product compatibility or functional complementarity.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Studies overconfidence under negative sampling and motivates generalized BCE as an independent objective ablation.
limitations: Does not establish that changing the loss will resolve the observed Electronics errors or improve pinned macro HR@10.
